mainTopic: Leaders, leaving ארץ ישראל in famine, the names of אלימלך's sons and רות's legacy, and the blessing of old produce
overview: This amud opens at the end of a lament over losing a great leader, and then teaches that even the smallest official is appointed by Heaven. רבי יהושע בן קרחה says אלימלך and his sons were not punished for leaving ארץ ישראל. Their sin was failing to pray for their generation. רבי יוחנן rules that if money itself is scarce, one may leave ארץ ישראל even when food prices are fairly low. He backs this with a memory of starvation in טבריה, then adds more memories of hunger, plenty and holiness. The גמרא then discusses the two sets of names for אלימלך's sons, מחלון and כליון or יואש and שרף, where רב and שמואל disagree. Two ברייתות on פסוקים in דברי הימים support one view and teach that רות lived to see the kingdom of שלמה. The פרק ends with the blessing of plenty: old grain that lasts without worms or blight and improves with age, and רב פפא's rule that old things are better except dates, beer and small fish.

steps.title: Woe to the ship that lost its captain
steps.stepSummary: The end of a lament: the world has lost its leader, like a ship that has lost its captain.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...its leader, and woe to the ship that has lost its captain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a sentence that started on the previous page. It mourns the loss of a great leader by comparing the world to a ship without a captain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison shows how much a generation depends on its leader. A ship without a captain drifts into danger, and a world without its great leader is in the same position. This sets up the next step, which is also about leaders.

phrases.english: its leader,
and woe to the ship that has lost its captain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a statement begun before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Losing a great leader leaves the world like a ship without its captain.

steps.title: Even a minor official is appointed by Heaven
steps.stepSummary: רב reads the פסוק 'You are exalted as head above all' to mean that even the person in charge of irrigation ditches gets his job from Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And You are exalted as head above all': רב חנן בר רבא said in the name of רב: Even the one in charge of the irrigation ditches is appointed from Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: Still on the subject of leaders, the גמרא quotes a פסוק and רב's teaching that every position of authority comes from Heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says ה׳ is 'head above all', which means He decides who becomes a head over others. רב picks the smallest job he can think of, the man over the water channels, to show that this applies to every level of authority.

keyTerms.meaning: The One Who is exalted, raised up
The official over the irrigation channels

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that any authority, big or small, is given by ה׳, so a leader should feel responsible to Him.

phrases.english: "And You are exalted as head above all":
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 29:11

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chanan bar Rava said in the name of Rav:
Even the one in charge of the irrigation ditches
phrases.notes: Literally 'head of the water channels,' a very small job. That's exactly רב's point.

phrases.english: is appointed from Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא אָמַר רַב: אֲפִילּוּ רֵישׁ גַּרְגּוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of leadership with a new teaching drawn from a פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every position of authority, even the smallest, is appointed by Heaven.

steps.title: They would never have left over hunger alone
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן קרחה rejects the idea that אלימלך and his sons were punished for leaving ארץ ישראל. He says they would have stayed even if all they had to eat was bran.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אבין said in the name of רבי יהושע בן קרחה: Heaven forbid! Even if they had found only bran, they would not have left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier explanation that אלימלך and his sons were punished for leaving ארץ ישראל, and רבי יהושע בן קרחה pushes that explanation away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי שמעון בן יוחי said they were punished for leaving the land. רבי יהושע בן קרחה says such great people would never have left over ordinary hunger. Even the poorest food, bran, would have kept them there, so they must have left only out of real danger.

keyTerms.meaning: Bran, the husks of grain; the poorest kind of food

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע בן קרחה is not saying leaving ארץ ישראל is fine. He is saying אלימלך and his family did not leave wrongly, so their punishment must have a different reason.

phrases.english: Rav Chiyya bar Avin said
in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha:
Heaven forbid!
phrases.notes: Heaven forbid that אלימלך and his sons sinned by leaving ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: For even if they had found bran, they would not have left.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ מָצְאוּ סוּבִּין – לֹא יָצְאוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the leadership theme and returns to the earlier discussion of why אלימלך and his sons were punished
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the earlier claim that leaving ארץ ישראל was the cause of their punishment
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Such righteous leaders would not have left over ordinary hunger, so leaving could not have been their sin

steps.title: So why were they punished?
steps.stepSummary: Once leaving the land has been ruled out as the sin, רבי יהושע בן קרחה asks what the real reason for the punishment was.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, why were they punished?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup question. It opens the way for רבי יהושע בן קרחה to give his own reason in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once leaving the land is no longer the reason, there is a gap: the family was clearly punished, so for what? The question shows that the punishment itself is not in doubt, only its cause.

phrases.english: But then, for what reason were they punished?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the rejection: if leaving was not the sin, what was?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The true reason אלימלך and his sons were punished

steps.title: They failed to pray for their generation
steps.stepSummary: They were punished because, as leaders, they should have prayed for mercy for their generation and did not. A פסוק in ישעיהו supports this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they should have asked for mercy for their generation, and they did not ask, as it says: 'When you cry out, let your gathered ones save you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן קרחה answers his own question. Their sin was not praying for the people, and he backs this up with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new idea is that leaders are responsible for the whole generation. The פסוק links crying out in prayer with being saved together with one's community. Since they did not cry out for the people, they were held responsible.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהושע בן קרחה, אלימלך and his sons were punished not for leaving ארץ ישראל but for failing, as leaders, to pray for their generation.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that leaders carry responsibility for their community's welfare through prayer, not only through action.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶן לְבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים עַל דּוֹרָם, וְלֹא בִּקְּשׁוּ –
phrases.english: Because they should have asked for mercy for their generation, and they did not ask,
as it says: "When you cry out, let your gathered ones save you."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 57:13

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶן לְבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים עַל דּוֹרָם, וְלֹא בִּקְּשׁוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They were punished for not praying for mercy for their generation, as supported by ישעיהו 57:13

steps.title: When one may leave even at lower food prices
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן limits the earlier rule about leaving ארץ ישראל in a famine. It applies only when money is easy to earn. If money itself is scarce, one may leave even when four סאה cost a סלע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: They taught this only when money is cheap and produce is expensive. But when money is expensive, even if four סאה cost a סלע, one may leave.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן narrows the earlier ברייתא, which allowed leaving the land only when food was very expensive (two סאה for a סלע).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא measured hardship by the price of grain. רבי יוחנן adds that the real question is whether people can afford food. If money is hard to earn, then even a fairly low price like four סאה for a סלע is out of reach, and one may leave to survive.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this (rule) in the case of...
Money is cheap, meaning easy to come by

steps.confusionAlert: 'Money is expensive' does not mean prices are high. It means money itself is scarce and hard to earn.
steps.whatToRemember: The היתר to leave ארץ ישראל in hard times depends on whether people can actually afford food, not only on the price of grain.
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the practical rule for when one may leave ארץ ישראל because of economic hardship.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
They taught this only
phrases.notes: He means the earlier ברייתא: you may leave ארץ ישראל only when two סאה cost a סלע.

phrases.english: when money is cheap and produce is expensive;
but when money is expensive,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ עָמְדוּ אַרְבַּע סְאִין בְּסֶלַע, יוֹצְאִין.
phrases.english: even if four se'ah stood at a sela, one may leave.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא מָעוֹת בְּזוֹל, וּפֵירוֹת בְּיוֹקֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the halachic ברייתא about leaving ארץ ישראל in a famine and limits its scope
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two-סאה-for-a-סלע limit applies only when money is easy to earn; when money is scarce, one may leave even at four סאה for a סלע.

steps.title: Food was cheap, but people starved because no one had a coin
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן remembers a time in טבריה when four סאה cost only a סלע, yet many people were swollen from hunger because they did not have even an איסר.
steps.simpleTranslation: (A memory list: סלע, laborer, carob, boy, they would say.) As רבי יוחנן said: I remember when four סאה sold for a סלע, and still many people in טבריה were swollen from hunger, because they did not have even an איסר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real-life memory of רבי יוחנן that shows his rule from step 6 in action. It also opens a list of his memories with a memory-aid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Four סאה for a סלע is a cheap price, so this was not a food shortage. The problem was that people had no money at all. This is exactly the case where רבי יוחנן said a person may leave ארץ ישראל: when money itself is scarce.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory-aid: a short list of keywords that helps you remember the order of the statements that follow
A measure of volume for grain or produce
A coin of fairly large value

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that 'famine' is about whether people can afford food, not only about the price of food.

phrases.english: (A memory-aid: Sela, laborer, carob, boy, they would say.)
phrases.notes: Each word stands for one of the memories coming up, in order.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
I remember when there would stand (be sold)
four se'a for a sela;
and yet many were swollen from hunger in Tiberias,
because there was not even an issar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life example of step 6's rule about leaving when money is scarce.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that one may leave even when four סאה cost a סלע, if money is scarce
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's own memory of starvation in טבריה despite low prices

steps.title: Laborers refused to work on the east side of the city
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן remembers that hungry laborers would not take jobs on the east side of the city, because the smell of bread would kill them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: I remember when laborers would not hire themselves out on the east side of the city, because they would die from the smell of the bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the list with another memory of hunger from רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The workers were so starved that even smelling bread they could not have was deadly for them. This adds another picture of how bad hunger was in those days.

keyTerms.meaning: Hire themselves out, take a job
The east side of the city

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: I remember
when laborers would not hire themselves out
on the east side of the city;
they would die from the smell of the bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second memory of hunger to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hunger was so severe that even the smell of bread could kill a starving worker.

steps.title: Memories of great plenty: honey-filled carobs and a fat-dripping raven
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן remembers a carob so full of honey that it ran down a child's arms. רבי אלעזר remembers meat so fatty that oil dripped from a wall to the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: I remember when a child would break a carob, and a line of honey would run over both his arms. And רבי אלעזר said: I remember when a raven would take meat, and a line of fat would run from the top of the wall down to the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The list now turns from hunger to the opposite: memories of how rich and plentiful the food once was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The carob shows how sweet and full the fruit of the land was. The raven's meat shows how fat the animals were. Both describe a time of great blessing, a contrast to the starving years in the previous memories.

keyTerms.meaning: A thread or line (here, a stream of liquid)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: I remember
when a child would break a carob;
and a line of honey would stretch
over his two arms.
And Rabbi Elazar said: I remember
when a raven would take meat;
and a line of fat would stretch
from the top of the wall down to the ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: נְהִירְנָא כַּד הֲוָה בָּצַע יָנוֹקָא חָרוּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from memories of hunger to memories of plenty.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In earlier times the produce and animals of the land were extremely rich.

steps.title: Teenagers walked together in the market and did not sin
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן remembers when boys and girls of sixteen and seventeen walked in the market together and did not sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: I remember when a boy and a girl of sixteen and seventeen would walk in the market, and they would not sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The list continues with a memory about the moral level of earlier times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This memory is about holiness, not food. Young people at an age of strong temptation could be together in public and still behave properly.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: I remember

phrases.aramaic: כַּד הֲווֹ מְטַיְּילִין טַלְיָא וְטַלְיְיתָא בְּשׁוּקָא
phrases.english: when a boy and a girl would walk in the market

phrases.aramaic: כְּבַר שֵׁית עֶשְׂרֵה וּכְבַר שַׁב עֶשְׂרֵה,
phrases.english: at sixteen and at seventeen years old,
and they would not sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: נְהִירְנָא כַּד הֲווֹ מְטַיְּילִין טַלְיָא וְטַלְיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a memory about moral purity to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In earlier generations young people kept themselves from sin even when mixing in public.

steps.title: A saying from the בית מדרש about trusting the authorities
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן remembers a saying from the בית מדרש: whoever goes along with them falls into their hands, and whoever relies on them loses what is his to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: I remember when they would say in the study hall: whoever agrees with them falls into their hands; whoever relies on them, what is his becomes theirs.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last item in רבי יוחנן's list of memories, a piece of practical advice he heard in the בית מדרש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The message is to be careful. Making deals with powerful outsiders or depending on them ends up putting you under their control and costing you what you own.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's list starts with hunger (which supports his rule about leaving ארץ ישראל). It then moves through memories of plenty and holiness and ends with a warning saying.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: I remember
when they would say in the study hall:
one who agrees with them falls into their hands;
phrases.notes: The text doesn't say who 'them' is. It's usually understood as the non-Jewish rulers.

phrases.english: one who relies on them, what is his becomes theirs.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: נְהִירְנָא כַּד הֲווֹ אָמְרִין בֵּי מִדְרְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the list of רבי יוחנן's memories.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Going along with or relying on them leads to losing oneself and one's property to them.

steps.title: אלימלך's sons have two different sets of names
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the story of רות. It points out that one פסוק calls the sons מחלון and כליון, while another calls them יואש and שרף.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written: 'מחלון and כליון', and it is written: 'יואש and שרף'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to אלימלך's family and raises a puzzle: the same two sons seem to have two pairs of names. This sets up the argument between רב and שמואל in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes both פסוקים describe the same two men who lived in מואב. So it needs to know which names are the real ones and why they have the other names too.

keyTerms.meaning: The names of אלימלך's sons in מגילת רות
The names in דברי הימים that the גמרא understands as the same two people

phrases.english: It is written: "Mahlon and Chilion,"
phrases.notes: רות 1:2

phrases.english: and it is written: "Joash and Saraph" —
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 4:22, which describes them as having ruled in מואב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבי יוחנן's memories and returns to the story of אלימלך's family.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which pair of names is the sons' real name, and why are they called by the other pair?

steps.title: One view: their real names were מחלון and כליון
steps.stepSummary: One of רב and שמואל says the real names were מחלון and כליון. They were called יואש because they gave up on the redemption, and שרף because they deserved burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל disagree. One says: their names were מחלון and כליון. So why were they called שרף and יואש? יואש, because they gave up hope of the redemption. שרף, because they became liable to burning before God.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first answer to the puzzle: מחלון and כליון are the real names, and יואש and שרף are nicknames that describe what they did wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each nickname is read as a play on words. יואש sounds like נתיאשו, 'they gave up hope', and שרף sounds like שריפה, 'burning'. The second names are a hidden criticism of the sons.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not tell us whether this view belongs to רב or to שמואל. It only says 'one says' and 'the other says'.

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel disagree;
one says: Mahlon and Chilion were their names,
and why were they called by the names Saraph and Joash?
Joash, because they gave up hope of the redemption,
Saraph, because they became liable to burning before God.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12's puzzle with the first opinion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The real names are מחלון and כליון. יואש and שרף are nicknames for giving up on the redemption and deserving burning.

steps.title: Other view: their real names were יואש and שרף
steps.stepSummary: The other one says the real names were יואש and שרף. They were called מחלון because they made their bodies profane, and כליון because they deserved destruction.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one says: their names were יואש and שרף. So why were they called מחלון and כליון? מחלון, because they made their bodies profane. כליון, because they became liable to destruction before God.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the opposite answer: יואש and שרף are the real names, and מחלון and כליון are the nicknames that describe their sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view flips the first one. Now the names in רות are the hidden criticism. מחלון sounds like חולין, 'profane', and כליון sounds like כליה, 'destruction'. Both sides agree the sons sinned; they only argue over which names were given and which were earned.
steps.whatToRemember: רב and שמואל agree that one pair of names describes the sons' sin. They argue only over which pair is the real name and which is the nickname.

phrases.english: And one says: Joash and Saraph were their names,
and why were they called by the names Mahlon and Chilion?
Mahlon, because they made their bodies profane,
and Chilion, because they became liable to destruction before God.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion to step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The real names are יואש and שרף. מחלון and כליון are nicknames for profaning their bodies and deserving destruction.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the view that מחלון and כליון were the real names
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says a ברייתא supports the opinion that the real names were מחלון and כליון. It begins quoting the ברייתא, which asks about a פסוק in דברי הימים.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a ברייתא that fits the opinion that their names were מחלון and כליון. It asks: what does this פסוק mean? 'And יוקים, and the men of כוזבא, and יואש and שרף, who ruled in מואב, and ישובי לחם, and the matters are ancient.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא announces that a ברייתא supports the opinion in Step 13, then quotes the פסוק that the ברייתא will explain. This is setup: the actual proof comes a few lines later, in Step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said the real names were מחלון and כליון, and יואש and שרף were only nicknames. Step 14 said the opposite. The ברייתא will treat יואש and שרף as hidden references to מחלון and כליון, and that backs Step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא teaches in line with the one who says
what is the meaning of what is written

phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא in line with the one who says
that Machlon and Kilyon were their names
As it is taught: What is the meaning of what is written:
"And Yokim, and the men of Kozeva,
and Yoash, and Saraf, who had dominion in Moav;
and Yashuvi Lechem; and the matters are ancient."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 4:22

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings outside support for one side of the disagreement in Steps 13–14
steps.raayaObject: The opinion that the real names were מחלון and כליון
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא explaining דברי הימים א 4:22

steps.title: יוקים is יהושע and the men of כוזבא are the people of גבעון
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains the first words of the פסוק. יוקים is יהושע, who kept his oath to the people of גבעון. The men of כוזבא are the people of גבעון, who lied to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And יוקים' is יהושע, who kept the oath to the people of גבעון. 'And the men of כוזבא' are the people of גבעון, who lied to יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts explaining the פסוק word by word. It ties each name to a person through a word that sounds like it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יוקים sounds like הקים, 'kept', so it points to יהושע keeping his oath. כוזבא sounds like כזבו, 'lied', so it points to the people of גבעון, who tricked him. The ברייתא reads these names as hints, not as ordinary family names.

phrases.english: "And Yokim": this is Yehoshua,
who kept the oath to the people of Givon.
phrases.notes: הקים (kept) sounds like יוקים. That sound link is the whole point.

phrases.english: "And the men of Kozeva": these are the people of Givon,
who lied to Yehoshua.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the פסוק quoted in Step 15
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יוקים refers to יהושע, and the men of כוזבא refer to the people of גבעון

steps.title: יואש and שרף are nicknames for מחלון and כליון
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says יואש and שרף are מחלון and כליון. They were called יואש because they gave up on the redemption, and שרף because they deserved burning before ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And יואש and שרף' are מחלון and כליון. Why were they called יואש and שרף? יואש, because they gave up on the redemption. שרף, because they deserved burning before ה׳.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the actual proof. The ברייתא calls יואש and שרף nicknames for מחלון and כליון, which matches the opinion in Step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא asks, 'Why were they called יואש and שרף?' That question only makes sense if those were not their real names. So the real names must be מחלון and כליון, just as Step 13 said.

keyTerms.meaning: and why were they called by this name

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא treats יואש and שרף as nicknames that need explaining. This supports the view that מחלון and כליון were the real names.

phrases.english: "And Yoash and Saraf": these are Machlon and Kilyon.
And why were they called by the names Yoash and Saraf?
Yoash, because they gave up on the redemption;
Saraf, because they deserved burning before ה׳.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and reaches the part that proves Step 13's view
steps.raayaObject: The real names were מחלון and כליון
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא asks why they were called יואש and שרף, so it treats those as nicknames

steps.title: They married Moabite women, and רות returned to בית לחם
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains 'who ruled in מואב' as marrying Moabite women. It explains 'ישובי לחם' as רות, who returned and attached herself to בית לחם יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Who ruled in מואב' means they married Moabite women. 'And ישובי לחם' is רות the Moabite, who returned and attached herself to בית לחם in יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going through the פסוק, now explaining the next two phrases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בעלו can mean 'ruled' but also 'took as wives', so it points to the marriages in מואב. ישובי sounds like שבה, 'returned', and לחם points to בית לחם. Together they hint at רות coming back with נעמי.

phrases.english: "Who had dominion in Moav": that they married Moabite women.
"And Yashuvi Lechem": this is Ruth the Moabite,
who returned and attached herself to Beit Lechem of Yehudah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲשֶׁר בָּעֲלוּ לְמוֹאָב שֶׁנָּשְׂאוּ נָשִׁים מוֹאָבִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the same פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק hints at the marriages to Moabite women and at רות joining בית לחם

steps.title: These matters were planned by ה׳ from long ago
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains 'the matters are ancient' to mean that ה׳, the Ancient of Days, said them. It shows this by linking the word 'found' used about דוד with the same word used about the daughters of לוט.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the matters are ancient': the Ancient of Days said these matters. It is written, 'I found דוד My servant,' and it is written, 'your two daughters who are found.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the פסוק. It says this whole story, including רות coming from מואב, was part of ה׳'s plan from long ago.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word 'found' appears about דוד and about the daughters of לוט. That ties דוד's beginnings all the way back to לוט's daughter, the mother of מואב. So רות, a Moabite, joining the Jewish people was planned long before it happened.

keyTerms.meaning: the Ancient of Days (a name for ה׳)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Ancient' here does not just mean 'old stories'. The ברייתא reads it as 'spoken by the Ancient One', meaning ה׳ planned these events.

phrases.english: "And the matters are ancient": these matters
the Ancient of Days said them;
phrases.notes: Ancient of Days is a name for ה׳.

phrases.english: as it is written: "I have found David My servant,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 89:21

phrases.english: and it is written: "Your two daughters who are found."
phrases.notes: בראשית 19:15. The shared word 'found' links דוד back to לוט's daughters.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַדְּבָרִים עַתִּיקִים דְּבָרִים הַלָּלוּ עַתִּיק יוֹמַיָּא אֲמָרָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא's explanation of the פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The events leading to דוד, including רות the Moabite, were planned by ה׳

steps.title: The next פסוק: the potters are the sons of יונדב בן רכב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes the next פסוק in דברי הימים. It explains 'the potters' as the sons of יונדב בן רכב, who kept their father's oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'These were the potters, and those who lived among plantings and fences; they lived there with the king in his work.' 'These were the potters' are the sons of יונדב בן רכב, who kept their father's oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next פסוק and begins a new word-by-word explanation. This sets up the ending about רות in Step 22.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יוצרים, 'potters', sounds like נצרו, 'kept'. So it hints at the sons of יונדב בן רכב, who faithfully kept their father's command.

keyTerms.meaning: the sons of יונדב בן רכב

phrases.english: "These were the potters, and those who dwelt among plantings and fences;
with the king in his work they dwelt there."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 4:23

phrases.aramaic: ״הֵמָּה הַיּוֹצְרִים״ – אֵלּוּ בְּנֵי יוֹנָדָב בֶּן רֵכָב,
phrases.english: "These were the potters": these are the sons of Yonadav son of Rechav,
who kept their father's oath.
phrases.notes: נצרו (kept) sounds like יוצרים (potters).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next פסוק in the same section of דברי הימים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'The potters' refers to the sons of יונדב בן רכב

steps.title: The plantings are שלמה and the fence is the סנהדרין
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains 'those who lived among plantings' as שלמה, who was like a planting in his kingdom. It explains 'fences' as the סנהדרין, who fenced in the breaches of the Jewish people.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Those who lived among plantings' is שלמה, who was like a planting in his kingdom. 'And fences' is the סנהדרין, who fenced in the breaks of the Jewish people.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues through the פסוק, now explaining 'plantings' and 'fences'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נטעים, 'plantings', is compared to שלמה's growing kingdom. גדרה, 'fence', sounds like גדרו, 'fenced in', and points to the סנהדרין, who repaired the gaps in the people.

phrases.english: "Those who dwelt among plantings": this is Shlomo,
who was like a planting in his kingdom.
"And fences": this is the Sanhedrin,
who fenced in the breaches of the Jewish people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the פסוק from Step 20
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Plantings' is שלמה and 'fences' is the סנהדרין

steps.title: רות lived to see the kingdom of שלמה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains 'with the king in his work they lived there' as רות. She lived to see the kingdom of שלמה, the grandson of her grandson. This is backed by the פסוק about a throne for the king's mother, which רבי אלעזר reads as the mother of the royal line.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'With the king in his work they lived there' is רות the Moabite. She saw the kingdom of שלמה, the grandson of her grandson. As it says, 'He set a throne for the king's mother,' and רבי אלעזר said: for the mother of the kingdom.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends by saying that רות lived long enough to see שלמה become king. It supports this with a פסוק and a teaching of רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רות was the great-great-grandmother of שלמה, yet the ברייתא says she was still alive in his time. 'The king's mother' is read as 'the mother of the kingdom', meaning רות, the mother of the royal family. So שלמה set a throne for her.

keyTerms.meaning: a throne for the king's mother
the mother of the kingdom (the royal line)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא ends by teaching that רות, the Moabite who joined the Jewish people, lived to see her descendant שלמה rule. She is called the 'mother of the kingdom'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This links back to Step 19: the Moabite roots of דוד's family were part of ה׳'s plan. רות saw that plan come true in the kingdom of שלמה.

phrases.aramaic: ״עִם הַמֶּלֶךְ בִּמְלַאכְתּוֹ יָשְׁבוּ שָׁם״ – זוֹ רוּת הַמּוֹאֲבִיָּה,
phrases.english: "With the king in his work they dwelt there": this is Ruth the Moabite,
who saw the kingdom of Shlomo,
the grandson of her grandson.
phrases.notes: רות's grandson was ישי, and ישי's grandson was שלמה.

phrases.english: As it is stated: "And he set a throne for the king's mother,"
phrases.notes: מלכים א 2:19

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: לְאִמָּהּ שֶׁל מַלְכוּת.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Elazar said: for the mother of the kingdom.
phrases.notes: He reads 'king's mother' as the mother of the whole royal family, meaning רות.

steps.triggerLanguage: עִם הַמֶּלֶךְ בִּמְלַאכְתּוֹ יָשְׁבוּ שָׁם זוֹ רוּת הַמּוֹאֲבִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the second ברייתא's explanation of the פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רות lived to see the reign of שלמה and is called the mother of the kingdom

steps.title: The old grain will be eaten without סלמנטון
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the פסוק 'and you shall eat of the old produce' as a promise that the old grain will be free of סלמנטון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: 'And you shall eat of the old produce' means without סלמנטון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about the blessing on old stored grain. It uses an unusual word, סלמנטון, which the גמרא will explain next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק promises that the grain from the sixth year will last until new grain grows. The ברייתא adds that this old grain will stay free of some kind of damage called סלמנטון. Steps 24 and 25 explain what that damage is.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught. This opens a ברייתא.
Old. Here it means stored produce from an earlier year.
A word for some kind of damage to stored produce. The גמרא explains it next.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"And you shall eat of the old produce"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:22

phrases.english: without salmanton.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, the blessing of plenty, after the ברייתות about the פסוקים in דברי הימים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The old grain promised in the פסוק will be free of סלמנטון.

steps.title: What does 'without סלמנטון' mean
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the word סלמנטון.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'without סלמנטון' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the strange word in the ברייתא means. This sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on the ברייתא. It is a plain request to define a word, so we know exactly what the blessing protects against.

keyTerms.meaning: What? Used to ask for an explanation.

phrases.english: What is "without salmanton"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a word in the ברייתא from Step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word סלמנטון.

steps.title: Worms or blight
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says סלמנטון means worms. רב ששת says it means blight.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: without worms. רב ששת said: without blight.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give two different meanings for the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב נחמן, the danger is worms that eat the grain until it is gone. For רב ששת, the danger is blight, which leaves the grain there but ruins its taste. The question is whether the blessing protects how much grain there is or how good it is.

keyTerms.meaning: Blight, a disease that spoils the taste of produce

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: Without worms.
And Rav Sheshet said: Without blight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב נחמן: free of worms. רב ששת: free of blight.

steps.title: A ברייתא that supports רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says each view has a ברייתא behind it. It starts with רב נחמן: the old grain will not be used up before the new grain is ready.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports רב ששת, and a ברייתא supports רב נחמן. The one that supports רב נחמן says: 'And you shall eat old.' One might think the Jews will have to wait for new grain because the old grain was used up. So the פסוק says 'until its produce comes,' meaning until the new grain comes on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first says that each אמורא has a ברייתא on his side. Then it quotes the one for רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא worries that the old grain might be 'used up' (כלה), which is what worms do. The פסוק promises that the old grain will last until the new crop is fully ready. That fits רב נחמן, who said the blessing is about no worms.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with him
So the פסוק says. This brings the proof from the פסוק.
On its own, in its natural time

phrases.english: It is taught in accordance with Rav Sheshet,
it is taught in accordance with Rav Nachman.
It is taught in accordance with Rav Nachman:
"And you shall eat old":
One might think the Jewish people will be waiting for the new,
because the old was used up?
The verse says: "Until its produce comes":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:22

phrases.english: until the produce comes on its own.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּוָתֵיהּ דְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת, תַּנְיָא כְּוָתֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the first of the two views in Step 25.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's view that סלמנטון means worms
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that worries the old grain will be 'used up' (שכלה).

steps.title: A ברייתא that supports רב ששת
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא says the old grain will not go bad before the new grain is ready. This fits רב ששת's view of blight.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports רב ששת: 'And you shall eat of the old produce.' One might think the Jews will have to wait for new grain because the old grain went bad. So the פסוק says 'until its produce comes,' meaning until the new grain comes on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that backs רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording is almost the same as the last ברייתא. The only change is the worry: the old grain might go 'bad' (רע) instead of being 'used up' (כלה). Going bad in taste is the damage blight causes, so this matches רב ששת.
steps.confusionAlert: The two ברייתות look almost the same. The only difference is one word: שכלה (used up, which is worms) or שרע (gone bad, which is blight).

phrases.english: It is taught in accordance with Rav Sheshet:
"And you shall eat of the old produce":
One might think the Jewish people will be waiting for the new
because the old went bad?
The verse says: "Until its produce comes":
until the produce comes on its own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the matching support for the second view in Step 25.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's view that סלמנטון means blight
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that worries the old grain will go 'bad' (שרע).

steps.title: Older produce will be better
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from 'ישן נושן' that any produce older than another of its kind will be better.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: 'And you shall eat old, very old' teaches that anything older than another of its kind will be better than it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another blessing from a different פסוק. Produce that has aged will actually become better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ברייתות promised that old grain would not spoil. This ברייתא goes further: age will make it better. The doubled word 'ישן נושן' (old, very old) is read as a promise of quality, not just of lasting.

keyTerms.meaning: Very old, kept for a long time

phrases.english: The Sages taught: "And you shall eat old, long kept":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 26:10

phrases.english: This teaches that anything that is older than its fellow
is better than its fellow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new פסוק, from the blessings in ויקרא 26, that gives a further blessing about old produce.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the time of blessing, older produce will be better than newer produce of the same kind.

steps.title: What about foods that are not usually aged
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know the blessing covers foods people do not normally store and age.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know this for things that people usually age. Where do we learn it for things that people do not usually age?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks whether the blessing is limited. This sets up the answer in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some foods, like wine, normally improve with age, so a blessing for them is no surprise. Other foods, like fruit, usually just go bad when kept. The ברייתא wants a source that the blessing reaches those foods too.

keyTerms.meaning: To age them, to store them over time
From where do we learn this?

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא דְּבָרִים שֶׁדַּרְכָּן לְיַישְּׁנָן;
phrases.english: And I have only things that are usually aged;
things that are not usually aged, from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא דְּבָרִים שֶׁדַּרְכָּן לְיַישְּׁנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far the rule of Step 28 reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, and from where, the blessing covers foods that are not normally aged.

steps.title: The doubled wording includes everything
steps.stepSummary: The doubled wording 'ישן נושן' teaches that the blessing covers every kind of food.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'old, very old': in every case.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that the extra word in the פסוק stretches the blessing to all foods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'ישן נושן' instead of only 'ישן' adds something. The ברייתא reads the extra word as 'in every case,' so even foods that usually spoil will improve with age.
steps.whatToRemember: The blessing on old produce has three parts. It will last until the new crop comes. It will not be harmed by worms (רב נחמן) or blight (רב ששת). And thanks to 'ישן נושן', every kind of food, even foods that usually spoil, will get better with age.

phrases.english: The verse says: "Old, long kept": in every case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The doubled word 'ישן נושן' includes all foods, even those not usually aged.

steps.title: So much produce that there is no room for the new
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains the end of the פסוק: storehouses full of old grain and threshing floors full of new grain, and people wonder how to clear one out to make room for the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: The words 'and you shall bring out the old because of the new' teach that the storehouses will be full of old produce and the threshing floors full of new produce. The Jewish people will say: How can we take this out to make room for that?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues its reading of the same פסוק and explains its last words. It describes the blessing as a problem of having too much food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last steps showed that the old produce will still be good, and even better, when the new crop arrives. This line adds the final picture. There is so much of both that people must empty the old produce out just to find space for the new.

keyTerms.meaning: You will take out or bring out
Storehouses where older produce is kept
Threshing floors, where the new harvest is gathered

steps.whatToRemember: The blessing of the פסוק is complete plenty. The old produce lasts, stays good, and is still around in such amounts that it has to be cleared away to make room for the new.

phrases.english: "And you shall bring out the old because of the new"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 26:10

phrases.english: teaches that there will be storehouses full of old produce
and threshing floors full of new produce,
and the Jewish people will say:
How can we take out this to make room for that?
phrases.notes: 'This' is the old produce in the storehouses, and 'that' is the new harvest waiting to come in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and reads the next words of the פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words 'וישן מפני חדש תוציאו' describe so much produce that the old has to be removed to make space for the new.

steps.title: Old things are better, except for three
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that anything old is better than new, except dates, beer, and small fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Everything old is better, except for dates, beer, and small fish.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a general rule that ties in with the ברייתא's idea that older produce is better. He also lists three exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא taught that whatever is older will be better. רב פפא states this as a rule about real life and points out that three items are better fresh. This is an exception to the rule, so the rule itself still stands.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Everything old is better,
except for dates, beer, and small fish.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter of 'One who sells a ship'
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for פרק הַמּוֹכֵר אֶת הַסְּפִינָה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'One who sells a ship'.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional line that marks the end of the פרק. It is not part of the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a farewell and a promise to come back and learn the פרק again. The סוגיא about ישן and חדש is the last discussion of this פרק.
steps.whatToRemember: פרק הַמּוֹכֵר אֶת הַסְּפִינָה ends with the blessing of plenty, where old produce lasts, improves, and fills the storehouses.
